subject: Interpreting results of stochastic character mapping

messages.author: 95e9261d3e867527
messages.subject: Interpreting results of stochastic character mapping
parts:
Hi!

I'm trying to understand the results of BioGeoBEARS::runBSM().

In particular I'm trying to determine at what time the events occurred.

The RES_ana_events_tables have several columns that sound like "time": time_bp, abs_event_time, event_time. The RES_clado_events_tables only have time_bp.

It appears that time_bp, abs_event_time, event_time are all different, just by doing a scatter plot showing each on the x or y axis.

If I want to use both of these in a downstream analysis, should I just use time_bp from each? What do the different times in RES_ana_events_tables mean?

Thanks!

Best,

Joel

messages.author: 115d05260b0c341a
messages.subject: Re: [BioGeoBEARS] Interpreting results of stochastic character mapping
parts:
Hi! Apologies this is confusing, I've never gotten a chance to document it all properly.

abs_event_time is absolute event time, this is usually what you want
event_time is IIRC the time along an individual branch
time_bp is the time-before-present of a node, the same as you would see in the tree table from prt(tree). The cladogenesis events always happen at the nodes.

Cheers!
Nick
